_readme: anchor-propagation-collateral, static probe of the HEAD export. Pairs: every city-anchors.json entry plus the Summarch and Penthelon literals in meshedWorldInit, matched by fold(name) to a maps_markers.json Settlements entry ("Lepon the Old" via the alias "Lepon"). Each row is a pair more than 3 px apart. Water test: the verbatim buildCityMask colour test (luma>=110 gives weight; r-b<=54 is water; radius-2 box blur on both; ratio>=0.5; only border-connected water kept), applied on the sampleCityMask window (ox=round((x-1.35r)*2), n=round(5.4r) z5 px, missing tiles filled rgb(198,178,128)). land_frac_footR = 1 - kept water inside the circle of radius FOOT_R[kind] world px (2r z5 px). Tiles are decoded by Pillow, not Chrome, so expect a small tolerance. Calibration: the Epēshu anchor reads nearest water SW 9.1 px at 212°, against stored SSW (202.5°) 10 px. nearest_sea_8way uses a WIDER window than sampleCityMask (±160 atlas px, the same test plus border connectivity) because stored distPx reaches 77 px; it gives the nearest kept-water pixel as an 8-way side, the exact bearing and the distance in atlas px. Side deltas are angular (degrees), because stored sides are 16-point. living_sea_mask_rule APPROXIMATES an unbuilt tool (tools/living-sea-mask.js does not exist yet): 1 mask px = 8x8 atlas px, water when >=50% of its signal pixels pass r-b<=54; Chebyshev neighbourhoods; harbor radius from the STORED sea.distPx (sea:null harbors use 2, the genCityCanvas default distPx 8). Only city-anchors.json entries are in scope as written. Approaches: segCircleHits + mergeAngles (0.25 rad) re-implemented at R=2.5*FOOT_R over party-route legs [prev,...via,cur] plus named-ways (land) and sea-lanes (sea). Bearings are compass degrees (0=N, clockwise); shift = nearest-match per anchor bearing; gained/lost = >20° from any bearing at the other position. visual_audit was read by eye from contact sheets of the z5 tiles. CAVEAT: the colour test cannot separate water from the olive/grey political region tints (tint r-b≈46-48 = gulf water r-b≈47). Where the marker footprint reads <30% land while sitting on a printed land dot, colour_test_reliable_here is false and the mask and living numbers there describe tint, not coast.

rows.offDot_reason: 0.9.7 (CHANGELOG + POLISH "Lake biome"): anchor moved off the wiki marker, which "floated mid-lake" (14% land), onto "the charted shore". Stale: 0.9.12 later moved the marker onto the printed ◉; the new anchor sits on a region-tint edge, not an inked shore.
rows.verdict_basis: The marker is on the printed ◉. The current colour test reads the olive region tint as water (tint r-b≈46-48, gulf water r-b≈47, test r-b<=54), so the ◉ footprint reads 2% land. Moving there with the mask unchanged gives a plan drawn almost all as water, the look 0.9.7 fixed. The 62% land at the current anchor is the untinted tan band N of the tint edge, so the shipped "lake" shore is the tint edge, not a shore. Mechanism (genCityCanvas, maps-site/index.html): Penthelon traits are harbor:true, sea:null, so the side comes from the branch `if(t.harbor&&!(t.sea&&t.sea.side)&&mask&&mask.water&&mask.bear)`. At the marker mask.water is true (0.98) but mask.bear is null, because the water centroid sits at the window centre. The side then falls back to the seeded `pick(Object.keys(COMPASS))`, and the 98%-water mask drowns the plan. At the current anchor bear="S" because the tint edge is the only "coast" in the window. Choices: (a) move and give the mask land/water from the ink coastline or the filigree DEM, which touches pinned sampleCityMask (UG3); (b) keep with a corrected offDot reason ("mask reads the Rhusagos tint as water"); (c) leave it until the Filigree land/water mask exists.
